purpose: Independent service review for Niigata official cadastral and parcel-oriented map sources.
assessment: Niigata has an evidenced official municipal public GIS. Its current public layer catalog was inspected, but only fixed-asset tax/land-price and sewer ledger sheet-index layers were exposed; no safe parcel geometry or stable native parcel identity was returned. Runtime readiness remains held.

attempts: Ran separate English and Japanese first-party discovery queries.
Fetched the official e-map viewer anonymously over TLS and followed its current JavaScript import/configuration.
Fetched the public layer catalog for mid=14; it returned four fixed-asset tax standard-residential-land/road-price layers with public WMS/tile metadata.
Fetched the public layer catalog for mid=30; it returned one sewer ledger map sheet-index layer.
Queried the exact immutable WUP point against the exposed mid=14 layer IDs 10502 and 9000000005 and mid=30 layer ID 30174; each returned HTTP 200 JSON [""] with no feature attributes.

Did not shift the WUP coordinate, log in, use credentials/private tokens, defeat access controls, request owner/titleholder/personal/contact/address/account data, or retain source-specific attributes.
Retained no GeoJSON because no safe parcel geometry and native identity were returned.

nextStep: Serial reviewer should independently re-run the current viewer and inspect any lot-number search route or documented cadastral export; qualify geometry, stable identity, CRS, and coverage before runtime admission.
remainingUncertainty: The viewer's lot-number search capability may use a route not exposed by the inspected thematic layer catalogs. Exact-point empty responses, map extent behavior, and the lack of a public parcel feature response do not prove citywide absence.
